newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's 6th TV channel for community - ABA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's 6th TV channel for community - ABA.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Monday it has recommended Australia's proposed sixth free-to-air television channel should used for community access television, preferably by government funding.
"Community access television has the greatest chance of success if it provides a wide coverage service," chairman Peter Webb said in a statement.

But, Webb said: "The costs involved in establishing and operating a high-power transmission facility, however, are too high for non-profit community access television services to raise on sponsorship alone."
Webb said with this factor in mind, ABA has recommended that the government should provide funding for community television transmission and programme production.
He said a Community Television Transmission Fund and a Community Television Production Fund should be set up, with both requiring continous government input for at least five years.

"If government funding is not forthcoming, the ABA considers that commercial involvement in community access television will be necessary. This will have to be done in a way which removes the problems faced by the trial community television services."
The ABA said it has also developed a non-government funded option, where a transmitter provider would enter into a contract arrangement with a community access television licensee.
It said the transmitter provider would meet the costs of transmission equipment and transmission operation in return for use of airtime on community access television.
The ABA said a third option is the continuation of the community television trial. This option would see the continued use of the sixth channel by the trial community television licensees.
"If adequate funding is not available, the ABA has recommended that sixth channel should be left vacant for review at a later date," Webb said.
Webb said the ABA's recommendation is contained in its report to the Communications Minister, Senator Richard Alston on the future use of the sixth channel.
The current free-to-air channels are the government-funded Australian Broadcasting Corp and the Special Broadcasting Service plus three commercial channels.
